apparatus.basis: Editor's restoration of standard Kephalaia narrative-frame opener ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ ⲡⲁⲭⲉϥ 'Once again he said' (cf. accumulated vocabulary).
Editor's restoration; ϣⲓ 'measure' completes idiom ⲉⲙⲛ̄ ϣⲓ ⲁⲣⲁϥ 'there is no measure to it.'
Editor's restoration completing Greek loanword ἐπιθυμία 'desire' across the line break (continued in line 17 as ⲙⲓⲁ).
Editor's restoration; ⲡⲉϥⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'his thought' (second of the five faculties per glossary), continuing the triplet desire-thought-love.
Editor's restoration of Greek ἀγάπη; the triadic 'desire of heart, thought, and love' frames the parents' affective stance toward their begotten child.

notes.decision: Rendered 'habitually disperses forth' — ϣⲱⲣ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'spread/scatter forth.' Captures the dispersive action of food into five offspring within the body. Habitual aspect ϣⲁⲥ- preserved.

Translated 'the breathing-out.' Lexeme appears related to ⲡⲱϣⲙⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ 'fragrant-breath' (in glossary) — the breath/exhalation. The first offspring of food rising 'through the breathing' to the mind fits the standard Manichaean physiology of food refining into pneumatic substance.

Rendered 'habitually pours forth.' The reduplicated ⲃⲁⲃ- likely an intensive form on ⲃⲱⲃ/ⲃⲱⲃⲉ-stem of pouring or spreading; the third offspring emerges via 'power and shame' — likely sweat/exudate of bodily exertion. Etymology not fully securable.

Translated 'the bodily offspring.' σωματικόν retains its Greek-philosophical force. The fifth offspring — the procreative bodily child fashioned in the flesh — is the only one the parents recognize, while the first four (breath, voice, sweat-substance, sexual emission) escape their notice.
Rendered 'the other four.' ⲕⲉ- 'other' + ϥⲧⲁⲩ '4' = 'the other four (offspring)' — distinguishing the four unrecognized offspring from the bodily fifth that the parents do recognize.
